notes.title: Development Update #4 - Backend Upgrades
notes.notes:
Hello,

I hope everyone has had a great start to the year. I said Wyoming Winter v1.13 would be out some time in February however I have decided to put a lot more effort into refactoring this update.

I am upgrading the Unity version Wyoming Winter uses from 2022 to Unity 6 LTS. This will bring Wyoming Winter's back end up to date with the newest Unity features and hopefully allow for some cool things to be done as well as allowing me to utilize new multiplayer development tools.

I am also fundamentally chaning the way the game is structured as the current structure is getting messy and convoluted due to lack of forwards thinking early on in the game's development life where I thought I'd be working on it for no more than 6 months.

This restructure is going to take time but will result in absoloutely massive productivity gains and speed ups in development. It will also hopefully allow for custom maps to be added a lot easier when I get round to that.

Please hold out for a bit longer on this update. I can promise it's worth it.

Cheers,
ValleyHound

notes.title: Development Update #3 - Vending Machine
notes.notes:
Hello,
This is the third development update, still regarding the up coming 1.13 update.

[h3]Vending machines[/h3]

I've been working on the new vending machine system I talked about at the end of my last development post and it's now implemented fully into the unreleased 1.13 version of the game. When you complete tasks you are now rewareded with an amount of cash based on how challenging (read : how exposed you are while completing and how long the task takes). This cash can then be used to purcahse items from vending machines which are scattered around the map. The vending machines have the same items for all players however one player purchasing an item and subsequently not being able to rebuy that item for the rest of the round does not mean that other players can't purchase that item although this is something I am going to be messing around with.

In the picture bellow you can see what vending machines look like
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43185341/94b857d24e7bf757f8546131abe4ac2740194b33.jpg[/img]

I will probably expose some of the vending machine variables in the game config which is editable at the start of a game (again coming in this update).

Right now I have a long list of ideas that may or may not be good as items in the game which I am working through and implementing and I'm hoping to get this whole update out before the 2 year anniversary of the game's release (December 9th).

This update will hopefully improve the gameplay to be a bit less repetative and boring. After this update I will be looking at new maps and new enemies / employee types that players can select from.

Building and releasing these updates does take a long time however for the most part the slow time is because this isn't my full time job or priority so bear with me on this.

Cheers,
ValleyHound

notes.title: Development Update #2 - The office upstairs
notes.notes:
Hello,
This is the second development update, still relating to the up coming 1.13 update. 

[h3]Upstairs[/h3]

Work recently has been going into fleshing out a second floor to the (currently only) office map. There is stair wells located throughout the exterior corridors of the map that lead into the 2nd floor of the office along with vents that allow players to navigate from upstairs to downstairs discreetly.

This step of fleshing out an upstairs is taking more time than anticipated as I want each room to be unique but I am at the same time running out of rooms that would make sense in the given setting without repetition, I am considering making the floor space upstairs smaller than downstairs.

See below a room from the 2nd floor called command. This is where the site director would be giving commands from were they still alive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43185341/fe2816fc1e467d793c7ac76d0ea33ef26863d4e9.png[/img]

[h3]Organisation[/h3]

Work has also been given to reorganising things behind the scene, as I said in the previous update a lot of time is and will be spent on refactoring the code base to reduce the amount of tech debt it currently faces. It has been nice to reap the rewards of this already as it makes debugging and developing new features noticeably faster and this is only from refactoring a few major components of the code base.

I previously had a long list of bugs and features I wanted to implement that were all written in a long text file called "Wyoming Winter TODO.txt" on my desktop. I've finally got around to binning this stupid file and setting up an organised board of tasks which will make things clearer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43185341/8eabe82f64ad4259d04b080f9b24c9bd21c2e64e.png[/img]

[h3]Task to Cash[/h3]

A new system I want to implement to make things more interesting is a store that you can go to during the game round and get weapons, utilities and funny items utilising cash that you gain from performing tasks which will replace the current very boring system of getting a pistol after completing all of your tasks.

Implementing this should make rounds a lot more variable and interesting so I will be extending the amount of time I'll be working on this update so that I can include this new system.

[h3]Game config[/h3]

In the course of revamping the game manager I decided to outsource all the game variables to a synced dictionary that would on the start of the round be populated with variables from a list of config names and values that are arranged into presets such as default gamelay or quicker round or less tasks. I'm going to allow the lobby host to modify a subset of these game config variables in a similar way to the sv_xxxxxxxxx commands you see in various Source engine games.

Thats it for right now.
Cheers,
ValleyHound

notes.title: Development Update #1 - 1.13 is coming
notes.notes:
TLDR - Work has been started on 1.13 and I hope to have it released in the coming months, it will bring a new map and remove a lot of tech debt from the code base which will allow me to develop new features faster.

Hello!

This is the first development update I'm going to post about Wyoming Winter, I plan to do these semi regularly. 

Work has started on version 1.13, my plan with this version is to remove a lot of tech debt that is currently stopping me from developing features that I think would help the game immensely and by doing so add a new map to acompany the current office map.

This update will take some time to finish I estimate around two months to develop, test and release but afterwards should lead the way to more frequent and higher quality updates.

I'll be fixing some issues in this update as well such as the jump movement tech that allows players to travel at immense speed around the map.

Player counts have been on the rise month after month with an increase in monthly Vivox (voice chat functionality) users by ~30% each month since January, this is very engouraging and I'm hopeful for the future growth of the playerbase.

If anyone has any suggestions please do reply or send a tweet to @ValleyHoundUK

Cheers,
ValleyHound

notes.title: Wyoming Winter - Now Available!
notes.notes:
Wyoming Winter, has finally been released on Steam! In this game, you and a group of fellow employees find yourselves snowed in to the Wyoming department of defence building as a blizzard covers the state. But you'll soon find out that your group is not the only thing trapped in the building.

As an employee, your job is to stop the Blight, an almost invincible, fast moving, dark creature, from escaping the facility. You'll need to help your fellow employees, complete risky lockdown tasks, and find a weapon to fight back.

Wyoming Winter is best played with 3-8 players, and servers are available in Europe, America, and Asia. So gather your friends and get ready! Hide in. Hold out. Don't be found.

Install Wyoming Winter on Steam now!
